title: Newsquawk Review 2026: Sign Up or Stay Away?
description: Newsquawk review: what its site claims about a $250 deposit, AI trading and a 4.6/5 rating, and what to check before you sign up.
author: Olivia Bennett
excerpt: Newsquawk promotes AI trading with a $250 minimum and a 4.6/5 rating, but names no operator or regulator.
content:
Newsquawk is presented as an AI-assisted trading platform with automated trades, a demo account and a $250 starting point. No operator, regulator or licence number is named on the page, and the single performance figure given is a 4.6/5 rating with no source.

The name suggests a news service, but the page sells trade signals and automated trading. Its asset table lists shares only. What the page states is set out below, along with the items we could not confirm independently.

Newsquawk at a Glance

Here is what the platform's own page states and what it leaves out.

CategoryWhat the page says
Platform typeAI-assisted trading with automatic and manual modes
Minimum deposit$250, currency not named
FeesNone stated. No schedule given
Payment methodsCards, PayPal, Skrill and bank transfer, with other options unnamed
WithdrawalsUsually within 24 hours. No limits given
SupportDescribed as 24/7, with no channels listed
Regulator or licenceNot stated
OperatorNot named

Items come from the platform's own page. We have not tested the platform.

Is Newsquawk Legit? What the Claims Show

Signal generation and automatic trades

The page says AI and machine learning generate signals and can place trades automatically, with a manual mode for users who prefer control. The page leaves out the strategy, the model and the risk limits, so there is nothing on it that lets a reader test the claim.

Performance and ratings

The page refers to a high success rate and notable gains from a small deposit, but gives no return figures, time period, sample size or method. There is no named source and no review count attached to the 4.6/5 rating.

Asset coverage

The name suggests a news service, but the page sells trade signals and automated trading. Its asset table lists shares only. Prospective users cannot find out from the page which markets are genuinely tradable before they sign up.

Costs and Minimum Deposit

The page states a $250 minimum deposit and says there are no registration, transaction or withdrawal fees. No fee schedule, spread details or payment-provider charges are provided.

We measure the minimum deposit at 250 in the local currency: AUD 250 in Australia, GBP 250 in the UK, and EUR 250 in the EU. Currency is not named next to the $250 figure, so verify both the amount and the currency in the terms before you pay in.

Who Is Behind Newsquawk

The page names no legal entity, company number or address. Every sign-up button points to coinpulse.cc, a third-party domain, with no disclosure of any commission the publisher may earn from those links.

Is Newsquawk a Scam? Withdrawals and Complaints

Searches for Newsquawk often ask whether it is a scam, whether withdrawals work and whether there are complaints. Withdrawals are said to usually take a day, though the page sets out no limits, timelines or complaints procedure.

Prior to depositing, search for independent complaint records and reviews that cite their sources. Positive testimonials and ratings say nothing about how withdrawal requests are dealt with.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Find the legal company behind Newsquawk and check it against your national regulator's register.
  • A full written schedule of fees, spreads and withdrawal charges should be requested before you commit.
  • Demand dated and verifiable performance records in place of one overall rating.
  • Keep your first deposit as small as possible and run the demo account before going live.

What could go wrong

The main risk is an unnamed operator, because a user has no clear party to hold to account. Contradictions between the page's claims make that risk worse. The automation changes the mechanics of trading, not the chance that money is lost.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Newsquawk legit?

The site makes claims about Newsquawk but names no operator, regulator or licence number. Before depositing, look at the company registry and the regulator's register.

What is the minimum deposit for Newsquawk?

The $250 amount appears on the page without any currency being named. Verify the figure and the currency in the terms prior to making a payment.

Is Newsquawk regulated?

No regulator or licence is named, and the brokers referred to are not identified. Check the company behind the service on your national regulator's register.

Does Newsquawk charge fees?

The page says there are no fees, but gives no schedule for spreads, withdrawals or currency conversion. Read the full terms first.

Is the risk of losing money removed by automation?

No. The automation changes the mechanics of trading, not the chance that money is lost.

Our Verdict on Newsquawk

Newsquawk's page makes broad claims without naming an operator, a regulator or verifiable results. Our rating reflects these gaps. We will come back to it once the operator and its claims can be confirmed. Use only funds you can comfortably afford to lose.
